text:
Maya (eng): Quick follow-up from today's all-hands: when we pitch, should we lead with performance or cost? Also what single competitor should ICs mention in casual convos?

Morgan (CEO): Lead with the problem we solve: predictable production inference. That naturally covers performance + cost. For casual convos, use 'inference infra' as shorthand rather than naming a vendor.

Tariq (Head of Product): Agreed. For PLG, put a metric up front (e.g., latency SLOs or expected unit cost improvement). For enterprise decks, lead with security and deployment modes.

Vera (VP Eng): From engineering calls, customers react to tangible infra differences: batching, KV cache durability across rollouts, and smart routing/fallbacks. Those are the lines that reduce the "why not self-host" question.

Nina (strategy): Competitor framing: three buckets in our one-pager: 1) LLM APIs (ease + models), 2) cloud endpoints (scale + lock-in), 3) infra vendors (control). Tailor the comparison to buyer persona.

Sam (sales): Request: can we get a 1-page cheat sheet with two elevator lines (PLG + enterprise) and the competitor buckets? AEs will use it on intro calls.

Morgan (CEO): Action: Tariq + Nina, please produce the cheat sheet by Thursday. Also we'll tweak the site wording to "Serve models reliably at production scale" instead of the current phrasing.

Maya (eng): Nice. One-liner for "why not run on cloud GPUs?" suggestion: "You keep the model; we take care of the ops to make it fast, reliable, and cost-predictable."

Vera (VP Eng): + example: "We reduced tail latency by X and lowered token cost by Y in a customer pilot." Use real numbers in sales decks where available.

notes-bot: Follow-up doc posted -> /internal/all-hands/1777777777-notes :spiral_note_pad:

Sam (sales): Thanks — we'll test the lines in calls and report back.
